verses.text: Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he ruled for thirty-one years in Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the LORD's eyes. He followed the ways of his ancestor David and did not turn away from them to the right or to the left.

In the eighth year of his rule, while he was still young, he began to seek the God of his ancestor David. In the twelfth year he began to clean Judah and Jerusalem of the hilltop shrines, the Asherah poles, and the carved and metal idols.

While he watched, the people tore down the altars of the Baal gods. He cut down the incense altars above them. He smashed the Asherah poles and the carved and metal idols, crushed them to dust, and scattered the dust over the graves of those who had offered sacrifices to them.
He burned the bones of the priests on their own altars. In this way he made Judah and Jerusalem clean again.
He did the same in the towns of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, as far as Naphtali, and in the ruins around them.
He tore down the altars, crushed the Asherah poles and idols into powder, and cut down all the incense altars all over the land of Israel. Then he went back to Jerusalem.

In the eighteenth year of his rule, after he had cleaned the land and the temple, he sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the city governor, and Joah son of Joahaz, the record keeper, to repair the temple of the LORD his God.

They went to Hilkiah the high priest and gave him the money that had been brought to God's temple. The Levites who guarded the doors had collected it from the people of Manasseh, Ephraim, and the rest of Israel, and from all Judah, Benjamin, and the people of Jerusalem.
They gave it to the men in charge of the work on the LORD's temple. These men paid the workers who repaired and restored the temple.
They gave money to the carpenters and builders to buy cut stone, and wood for the supports and beams of the buildings the kings of Judah had let fall apart.

The men did the work faithfully. Their supervisors were Jahath and Obadiah, Levites from the family of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam from the family of Kohath. Other Levites, who were all skilled musicians,
were in charge of the workers who carried loads and directed all the workers in every job. Some Levites were secretaries, officials, and gatekeepers.
While they were bringing out the money that had been brought to the LORD's temple, Hilkiah the priest found the book of the LORD's law, given through Moses.
Hilkiah said to Shaphan the secretary, "I have found the book of the law in the LORD's temple." He gave the book to Shaphan.
Shaphan took the book to the king and reported to him: "Your officials are doing everything you told them to do.
They have emptied out the money that was in the LORD's temple and given it to the supervisors and the workers."
Then Shaphan the secretary told the king, "Hilkiah the priest has given me a book." And Shaphan read from it to the king.
When the king heard the words of the law, he tore his clothes.
He gave orders to Hilkiah, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah, Shaphan the secretary, and Asaiah, the king's servant:

"Go and ask the LORD for me and for the people left in Israel and Judah about what is written in this book that was found. The LORD's anger against us is great, because our ancestors did not obey the LORD's word. They did not do everything written in this book."

So Hilkiah and the men the king had sent went to the prophet Huldah. She was the wife of Shallum son of Tokhath, son of Hasrah, who was in charge of the royal clothes. She lived in the newer part of Jerusalem. They told her what had happened.
She said to them, "The LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Tell the man who sent you to me,
"The LORD says: Look, I am going to bring disaster on this place and the people who live here, all the curses written in the book that was read to the king of Judah.

They have left me and burned incense to other gods. They have made me angry with all the idols they have made with their hands. So my anger will be poured out on this place, and it will not be put out."'
But tell the king of Judah, who sent you to ask the LORD, 'The LORD, the God of Israel, says this about the words you heard:

Your heart was soft, and you humbled yourself before God when you heard what he said against this place and its people. You humbled yourself before me, tore your clothes, and cried in front of me. So I have heard you, says the LORD.
Look, I will let you die in peace and be buried with your ancestors. You will not see all the disaster I am going to bring on this place and its people.'" So they took her answer back to the king.
Then the king called together all the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem.

The king went up to the LORD's temple with all the people of Judah and Jerusalem, the priests, the Levites, and all the people, from the least to the greatest. He read aloud to them all the words of the book of the covenant that had been found in the LORD's temple.

The king stood in his place and made a covenant in front of the LORD. He promised to follow the LORD and to obey his commands, laws, and rules with all his heart and all his soul, and to do what the covenant written in this book said.
He made everyone in Jerusalem and Benjamin promise to keep it too. So the people of Jerusalem obeyed the covenant of God, the God of their ancestors.

Josiah removed all the disgusting idols from all the lands that belonged to the Israelites. He made everyone in Israel serve the LORD their God. As long as he lived, they did not turn away from following the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
